final_answer: I wrote `index.html` (about 16 KB) and checked it with Python's `html.parser`: it parsed with no errors, every tag that opens also closes, and it links to no outside files. It has everything you asked for. A sticky nav bar sits on top, followed by a hero section with a headline, two call-to-action buttons and a small drawn mock-up of the app. Next come a 6-card feature grid with inline SVG icons and a 3-tier pricing table (Starter $0, Pro $8 marked "Most popular", Team $15 per user). The FAQ has five questions that open and close using the built-in `<details>`/`<summary>` tags, so it needs no JavaScript. A colored sign-up banner and a four-column footer finish the page. All styling is in one `<style>` block inside the file, with no external fonts, images or scripts; a few small layout tweaks are `style` attributes on individual tags. Layouts adapt to screen size: at 960px and below, the hero stacks, features drop to two columns, pricing becomes one column and the footer two; at 640px and below, everything is one column and the nav links are hidden. The page also has a "skip to content" link, visible keyboard focus outlines and reduced animation for users who turn motion off. I haven't viewed it in a browser, so the visual layout and the breakpoints still need a look.
